fluff.overview: The Heavy APC is a twenty-ton combat transport designed to address the fundamental limitation of the standard Armored Personnel Carrier -- its ability to carry only a single infantry squad. By doubling the chassis weight, the Heavy APC provides six tons of infantry carrying capacity, sufficient for two full platoons of standard infantry or one platoon of motorized or jump troops. Produced in the same three motive configurations as its lighter counterpart, the Heavy APC offers substantially improved armor protection alongside its increased transport capacity, making it the largest dedicated personnel carrier in common service across the Inner Sphere.
fluff.capabilities:
The Heavy Hover APC carries six tons of infantry -- sufficient for two full platoons of standard foot infantry or one platoon of motorized or jump troops -- making it the largest hover-mobile personnel carrier in common service. An internal combustion engine propels the twenty-ton vehicle to a maximum speed of approximately one hundred thirty kilometers per hour, fast enough for rapid insertions though especially slower than the ten-ton standard hover APC. Two front-mounted machine guns provide anti-infantry defense during approach and withdrawal.

Fifty-six points of standard armor provide substantially better protection than the standard APC, though the design concentrates armor heavily on the front and flanks at the expense of the rear, which houses the assault ramp for troop deployment. The lack of a turret limits the machine guns to a forward-only firing arc, leaving the vehicle vulnerable to flanking attacks. This trade-off reflects the design philosophy of a vehicle that approaches the enemy head-on, deploys its infantry, and withdraws before lateral threats can develop.
fluff.deployment: The Heavy Hover APC serves with mobile forces across the Inner Sphere, particularly those formations requiring rapid deployment of infantry in strength. The Federated Commonwealth's Regimental Combat Teams fielded large numbers, using the hover variant's speed to rapidly insert two-platoon infantry formations in support of BattleMech advances. Post-Jihad successor states maintain the design in similar roles, valuing its ability to deliver meaningful infantry strength at hover speeds.
fluff.history:
The Heavy APC was developed in the twenty-fifth century as a direct response to the standard APC's limited carrying capacity. Military planners recognized that a single squad per vehicle was insufficient for rapid infantry deployment, particularly in combined-arms formations where infantry needed to arrive in strength alongside heavier units. The twenty-ton design entered service around 2470, predating the modern standard APC by several decades, and quickly became the preferred transport for mobile forces with large infantry contingents.

The Federated Commonwealth's Regimental Combat Teams made the Heavy APC a centerpiece of their combined-arms doctrine, fielding large numbers of all three motive types to rapidly deploy infantry in support of BattleMech and armor formations. Other Inner Sphere powers adopted the design in varying numbers, with the Free Worlds League and Draconis Combine favoring the tracked variant for its all-terrain capability, while the Lyran Commonwealth preferred the wheeled model for operations along its extensive road networks.

During the Jihad, the Word of Blake developed a specialized wheeled variant incorporating an extralight engine and heavy ferro-fibrous armor, significantly improving protection and speed while retaining full troop capacity. The Scout Tank conversion of the hover chassis, replacing the infantry compartment entirely with sensors and a light autocannon, demonstrated the platform's versatility beyond its original transport role. Like the standard APC, the Heavy APC's simplicity and reliability have kept it in continuous production and service for over six centuries.
